runs.text: Friday morning.
OpenAI is confidentially filing its IPO prospectus with the SEC today

— WSJ's scoop, with CNBC, Reuters, Axios, and Quartz independently confirming. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are running the deal. The company's last private valuation was $852B; the public framing of a trillion-dollar listing would make this the largest tech IPO in history. The confidential filing window means a public S-1 sits sixty to ninety days behind today, so the earliest visible prospectus lands in late July or August, and the company is
targeting Labor Day to Thanksgiving 2026
for the actual listing window.
Forty-eight hours earlier on the other side of the duopoly,
Anthropic told investors
— via the financing-document WSJ surfaced — that Q2 2026 will land at $10.9B in revenue, a 130% jump over Q1's $4.8B, with
$559M of first-ever operating profit

. Last summer's guidance said no full-year profitability until 2028 at earliest; that window just compressed by three years. Stock-based comp is excluded; model training cost is in. The growth rate currently outpaces the historical Q-over-Q peaks of Zoom, Google, and Facebook. Public listing open by year-end, October the most-cited window. The duopoly narrative is no longer about who's at the frontier — it's about who lists first.
Underneath the capital story,
Anthropic shipped two new pieces of agent infrastructure

at Code with Claude London (Wed-Thu). Self-hosted sandboxes (public beta): Claude Managed Agents now execute tool calls inside customer-managed environments — Cloudflare, Daytona, Modal, Vercel, or the customer's own infra.
MCP Tunnels (research preview)

: Claude agents reach private MCP servers behind enterprise firewalls without exposing those servers to the public internet — single outbound encrypted connection via a customer-deployed lightweight gateway. No inbound firewall changes required. The agent-orchestration plane stays on Anthropic; the execution plane is the customer's. This is the enterprise-grade architecture pitch — and the structural answer to the question every CIO has been asking about agent deployment governance.
Carry from Thursday catch-up: the
$15B/year Anthropic-xAI Colossus deal
is now widely understood.
Spotify's 4,500-deploys/day Claude story
continues to propagate as the reference enterprise customer.
@decodeddaily07's 'three labs, three scarcities' frame
still reads cleanly — and the IPO twin-filing this week is the most concrete possible expression of Anthropic and OpenAI's competing scarcity bets meeting the public markets at the same moment.
SP-Index +1 to 74. Capital substrate moved on twin IPO trajectory. Frontier release velocity moved on agent infrastructure ship. Everything else holds.

The structural read for Q3: public-markets discipline arrives at both labs in the same window. The next twelve months are the lock-up and lookahead window — and the singularity narrative writes itself in S-1 risk-factor sections.

loop_dispatch.closing_line: Two confidential filings, one duopoly. The singularity now has a ticker.

news.title: OpenAI confidentially files IPO prospectus TODAY — Goldman + Morgan Stanley underwriting, $852B → potential $1T listing
news.summary: OpenAI is confidentially filing its IPO prospectus with the SEC today, May 22, 2026. WSJ broke the story; CNBC, Reuters, Axios, and Quartz independently confirmed. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are running the deal. The company's last private valuation was $852B; commentary frames a trillion-dollar listing as the largest tech IPO in history. The confidential filing means a public S-1 will not surface for 60-90 days — earliest public prospectus lands late July or August. The actual listing window is Labor Day to Thanksgiving 2026 (4-6 months runway after confidential drop).
news.why_it_matters: Capital substrate as a curve dimension was added to the SP-Index this month for exactly this kind of event. OpenAI's IPO is the institutional-validation moment for the entire frontier-AI economy — and the timing (same week as Anthropic's $10.9B Q2 + first-profit projection) reframes both labs from research-and-talent stories into public-company stories. The next twelve months become the S-1 lock-up window: every research move, model release, and customer signing gets retold as material disclosure. The investor base on listing day will set the public valuation floor for all frontier AI — and price-discovery happens in real time.
news.verdict: Largest curve event of the week, possibly the quarter. Capital substrate +1.
news.evidence: WSJ first scoop (paywalled) + CNBC primary coverage (May 20) + Reuters + Axios + Quartz + Business Upturn.

news.title: Anthropic projects $10.9B Q2 revenue + $559M first operating profit — three years ahead of last summer's guidance
news.summary: WSJ published internal Anthropic financials shared with investors ahead of the next funding round. Q2 2026 revenue projection: $10.9B, up 130% from Q1's $4.8B. First operating profit ever: $559M. Stock-based comp excluded; model training cost included. The quarter-over-quarter growth rate currently outpaces the historical peaks of Zoom, Google, and Facebook. Last summer Anthropic told investors no full-year profitability before 2028 — that window just compressed by three years. The company is open to a public listing by year-end, with October 2026 the most-cited window.
news.why_it_matters: Anthropic and OpenAI are now both walking to the public markets in the same week. The growth-rate comparison to Zoom/Google/Facebook is the relevant SaaS-historical anchor — and Anthropic is outpacing the peak of each. Profitability arriving 3 years ahead of guidance is the second part of the story: the lab told investors not to expect this until 2028, then delivered in 2026. Capital-substrate-component value on the SP-Index needs to reflect both labs going public-market-track in the same window. The deeper signal: $40B+ Anthropic-xAI compute commitment makes more sense when Q2 revenue is $10.9B, not $4.8B. The math closes.
news.verdict: Capital substrate +1. The duopoly's profitability trajectory is now narrower than expected.
news.evidence: WSJ primary scoop (paywalled, May 20) + Investing.com + CryptoBriefing + Yahoo Finance + IndexBox + BitcoinWorld + WEEX.
news.tap_next: Watch for: (a) Anthropic's reaction to OpenAI's confidential filing; (b) whether the October IPO window holds or accelerates; (c) any commentary on the Mythos / Glasswing revenue contribution (currently ~50 vetted orgs, defensive cyber tier).

news.title: MCP Tunnels + self-hosted sandboxes ship at Code with Claude London — enterprise lock-down for Claude Managed Agents
news.summary: Anthropic shipped two enterprise-grade pieces of agent infrastructure at Code with Claude London this week. Self-hosted sandboxes (public beta): Claude Managed Agents now execute tool calls inside customer-managed environments — Cloudflare, Daytona, Modal, Vercel, or the customer's own infrastructure. MCP Tunnels (research preview): agents access private MCP servers behind enterprise firewalls without exposing those servers to the public internet. Single outbound encrypted connection via a customer-deployed lightweight gateway. No inbound firewall changes required. Neither breaks existing Claude Managed Agents integrations. The agent orchestration plane stays on Anthropic's servers; the execution plane is the customer's. This is the structural answer to every CIO's agent-deployment governance question.
news.why_it_matters: Frontier release velocity on agent-infrastructure tier. The MCP Tunnel architecture is the canonical pattern for enterprise agent deployment: agents reach internal databases and private APIs without security perimeter changes. Combined with Stainless absorption (Monday), Anthropic now owns the canonical patterns for: SDK generation, MCP server generation, MCP server access, and agent tool execution. The full developer-platform stack. Enterprise procurement cycles for Claude Managed Agents just shortened — the security review answer is no longer 'we'll need to figure that out.'
news.verdict: Frontier release velocity +1. Agent infrastructure is now Anthropic's full-stack play.
news.evidence: anthropic.com primary + The New Stack analysis + The Decoder + InfoQ + TestingCatalog + multiple secondary.
news.tap_next: Watch: (a) public-beta enterprise customer wins via Cloudflare/Daytona/Modal/Vercel — first reference logos; (b) MCP Tunnel research-preview to general-availability timeline; (c) competitive response from OpenAI / Google on agent infra.

news.summary: @kimmonismus posted his June read this morning (May 22, ~12 UTC): 'June will be huge. Gemini 3.5 Pro (confirmed), GPT-5.6 (rumored but pretty confident for a release). Still waiting for announcements: Claude Sonnet 4.8 (Claude-Code/Source-Map-Leak).' Boris Cherny, head of Claude Code, confirmed it was a 'plain developer error.' The leak surfaced Sonnet 4.8 as the next version with vision accuracy approaching 98% and coding benchmark +12 points over Sonnet 4.6.

The Gemini 3.5 Pro June slot (Sundar at I/O: 'Give us until next month') is confirmed; the GPT-5.6 read is rumor-mill consensus; the Sonnet 4.8 path is leak-confirmed but unannounced. If two of three ship in June, frontier-release-velocity component spikes again. If three of three ship — the most rumor-mill-consensus outcome — that's the largest frontier-release week of 2026.
news.verdict: Watch-shape. June calendar is now the structural fork.
